answer: A wharf is where strangers become neighbours, and that is where Sybil resistance should begin. Every new account must be sponsored at a public wharf by two established members who stake some of their own standing on it; a sponsor who vouches for a farm loses it. Add a glacier rule: a newcomer's stake thaws slowly, month by month, so buying many accounts is costly and slow to monetise. Finally, gale audits sweep a random slice of accounts, demanding fresh proof of unique control. One fake account is cheap; a sponsored, slowly thawing fleet caught in the same gale is not.
